title: Men! Whose Boast It Is That Ye
description: Men! Whose Boast It Is That Ye in Tonic Solfa to MARTYN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: James Russell Lowell wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 437, “Anti-Slavery Hymn”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens Double (7.7.7.7 D) (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MARTYN; any other Sevens Double (7.7.7.7 D) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Men! whose boast it is that ye Come of fa-thers brave and free, If there breathe on earth a slave, Are ye tru-ly free and brave? If ye do not feel the chain, When it works a broth-er's pain, Are ye not base slaves in-deed, Slaves un-wor-thy to be freed?

lines: Men! whose boast it is that ye
Come of fathers brave and free,
If there breathe on earth a slave,
Are ye truly free and brave?
If ye do not feel the chain,
When it works a brother's pain,
Are ye not base slaves indeed,
Slaves unworthy to be freed?
Is true freedom but to break
Fetters for our own dear sake,
And with leathern hearts forget
That we owe mankind a debt?
No! true freedom is to share
All the chains our brothers wear,
And with heart and hand to be
Earnest to make others free.
They are slaves, who fear to speak
For the fallen and the weak;
They are slaves, who will not choose
Hatred, scoffing, and abuse,
Rather than, in silence, shrink
From the truth they needs must think;
They are slaves, who dare not be
In the right with two or three.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Russell Lowell died in 1891.
credits: Words by James Russell Lowell (1819–1891), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MARTYN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
